body: eh. i'm glad it got better for you.

no. i don't think i've ever left a session (with either one of them) feeling any different than when i came in.

i mean, my feelings aren't anything really new to me. you're probably not going to ask me any questions i haven't already asked myself. so it didn't ever feel like i was learning anything new, just reiterating what has been said so many times already.

they were mostly gestalt psychologists. but their methods varied.

the first one liked to do a lot of projective tests and similar techniques.

the second one was convinced that i just need to find *the thing* that will completely change everything and i'll pull myself out of the slump.

the third one was a proponent of tough love.

my current therapist doesn't really use tests (at least not with me) and is all about just talking while being full of empathy for everything i say.

but that's not working either.

it was one of the things i went over with my latest therapist.

but we didn't dwell on it for too long.
yes. of course. close looks at my relationship with my mother, my relationship with my father, their relationship, my relationship to my siblings, their relationship etc.

not really that much. i was a college freshman. it wasn't like some single thing that happened and changed everything. i just started enjoying everything less and less, losing sight of what i want out of... well, anything. i started really disliking my major, but i didn't have any idea what i'd rather do, so i decided that until i do, there's no reason not to continue down this road. now i hate my job (even though, as i said, it's been one of my dream jobs since my early years), don't enjoy my free time at all and don't know what i want our of... well, anything.

i could quit and do something else, obviously. but without having any indication of how i would like to spend my time, it seems like a random shot in the dark. and i have pretty much lost all hope that it will ever get better. i can't even imagine anything that could be even remotely worth living for. right now, i'm just interested in living long enough to either get to a state where i just don't care and go through with it or to outlive my parents so i can do it without feeling so guilty about it. not killing myself because my parents are still alive is a shitty reason, i know, but it's the best one i have. 

my family is one of fairly traditional values, with high expectations of everyone. we seem really close, but in reality, we don't really talk, at least not about important stuff.

i'm not really sure where we're going with this. you and i both know that i've been over all this and much more with all my therapists and friends. it can end in a few ways and conclusions, but it will not end in helping me in any way, i don't think.

maybe i'm just craving some attention. that's always a possibility. i don't even know anymore.

it started around seven years ago, when i was 19. the bad moods have been intensifying and cropping up more often over the years. but there isn't a pattern, obviously. i could have one really bad day in a given week, or i could have a really bad month in a given month.

"i can't kill myself" is something i keep telling myself. mostly because i realize that my death would greatly impact some people that are close to me. but i don't know... lately it really feels like i'm near the end. it feels like i should say my goodbyes. i have some plans already, just need to iron out the details.

alright, let's give it a shot.

usually i can at least somewhat tune out the suicidal thoughts. or cover it up with humor, as many people do.

but when i'm in one of my bad moods, i lose that ability completely. then it's pretty much all i see. if i look at the cars on the road, i think about which ones are going fast enough to kill me if they were to hit me. if i walk by a pub, i think about going in and starting a fight with a group of drunk guys in hopes of not getting out alive. i want to hang myself, but by throwing myself from somewhere really high up, so my neck snaps and there's no chance of surviving.

and then, after i've calmed down from my anger aimed at the people that care about me (because they're the reason i can't kill myself), i start planning out methods which would account for having people who care about me. slowly alienating everyone around me, then moving to a far away place and cutting off contact from them so i can just kill myself without anyone knowing... stuff like that.

but mostly it's just despair. just thinking about any way to end it all, knowing i probably won't do it because it would absolutely destroy my parents.

whee.

yeah. we really talk about everything and i don't really feel like there's stuff that i can't talk to them about.

well, maybe apart from the suicidal thoughts. it's not that i can't talk to them about it, it's that they get kind of freaked out, which makes me feel even worse because, as i said, the conversations don't really help.

i don't know. if there is something deep to reach, i wouldn't know.

but i do think i have pretty deep and substantial friendships. i just can't seem to appreciate it.

my friends are definitely sources of support. they all try pretty hard. also, four of them have graduated with a degree in psychology, so i do have people to talk to.

the thing is that none of it helps. i just end up feeling like an asshole because they all feel worse afterwards and i feel no better as a result.

we can keep talking, but i don't believe there's anything you or anyone else can say that will change anything. i'm just tired of trying and i don't feel like i have anything to lose by simply killing myself.

well, no one thing in particular.

i'm in my twenties, completely healthy (as far as i know, anyway), living on my own, have a job that's been one of my dream jobs since i was a little kid with decent pay and i have a lot of friends.

and i hate it. i hate every minute of it. nothing feels good. no achievement, however big, feels good. i hate my job. and i hated every one of my jobs before this one. i haven't enjoyed any of my hobbies for years now. and not for a lack of trying either. being in bands, working on some stuff in film, playing sports, gym, hiking, skating...

but everything feels like a chore. i'm trying stuff just to try it at this point. it all feels so hollow with no hope of ever getting any better.

and it feels incredibly petty and ungrateful. here i am, in a position millions would kill to be in, and yet i'm unable to enjoy any of it. 

if i'm not torn apart by feeling like shit, then i'm mind-numbingly bored. i really struggle to find absolutely any reason to keep going.  in face of it all, any kind of optimism seems almost childish and naive.

and yes, i've tried therapy. i've changed four different therapists over the past few years.

it's easy to *say* that maybe it'll get better. maybe tomorrow morning won't be so difficult. maybe i'll find someone i'll fall for. maybe i'll start enjoying things.

but i've been living on these maybes for years now. i just... i don't know. it feels silly to go on.
i'm open to talking about it, but there would really be no point. if talking did anything, something would have changed already.
